title: Conditional types (T extends U ? X : Y)
hook: Conditional types pick one of two type expressions based on whether T is assignable to U — the foundation for ReturnType, Exclude, and non-nullable T. Senior interviews build from T extends U ? X : Y to infer and distributive rules.

blocks.text: A **conditional type** has the form **`T extends U ? X : Y`**. The compiler checks if **T** is assignable to **U**; if yes, the result is **X**, otherwise **Y**. Nested conditionals build complex logic. **`infer`** (next topic) works only inside the `extends` clause. Conditional types are **pure compile-time** — they erase completely in JavaScript output.

entries.plainDefinition: Type-level if-then-else: T extends U ? X : Y.
entries.example: type IsNumber<T> = T extends number ? true : false

entries.plainDefinition: Checks assignability — wider than runtime instanceof.
entries.example: string extends string ? yes : no → yes

entries.plainDefinition: When T is a naked union, conditional distributes over each member.
entries.example: T extends string ? A : B over string|number

entries.plainDefinition: Wrap T in tuple [T] to prevent distribution over union.

blocks.text: Utility types in lib.d.ts are conditional types: **Exclude<T, U>**, **Extract<T, U>**, **NonNullable<T>**. Library APIs use conditionals for overload-like behavior without runtime branches. Misunderstanding **distributivity** causes surprise when `T extends string ? A : B` applied to `string | number` becomes `A | B` not a single branch choice.

blocks.title: extends means assignable
blocks.body: T extends U uses TypeScript assignability — { x: number } extends { x: number } is true; class hierarchy and union rules apply.

blocks.title: Unexpected distributivity
blocks.body: Conditional over union distributes — use [T] extends [U] when you need to test the whole union at once.

blocks.title: Runtime ternary confusion
blocks.body: Conditional types never emit code — runtime if still needed for unknown values.

blocks.text: Build Exclude, Extract, NonNullable in interview. Chain to infer for ReturnType. Explain why `T extends any` distributes. Read lib.es5 utility definitions. Production: conditional types in generic fetch client mapping endpoint keys to response types. Stop when readability drops — module 15 limits.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Cannot write Exclude. Confuse runtime ternary with type conditional. No mention of distribution. Saying conditionals run at runtime.

interviewTakeaways: T extends U ? X : Y — assignability check picks branch.
60s: Type-level if. extends means assignable. Distributes over naked union. infer in extends for extraction. Erased at runtime.
commonPitfalls: Weak: ignore distribution on string | number
Strong: 'Exclude distributes. [T] wraps to disable. NonNullable filters null. All compile-time.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript value ? a : b runs at runtime; conditional types are the compile-time parallel for type transformation.
Conditional types plus infer power ReturnType, Awaited, and Parameters — next step after basics.
